units.title: Water Resources and Quality in the 21st Century
units.topics: • Global and Indian water scenario: availability, demand, water scarcity, and water footprint. • Climate change impacts on water resources: altered monsoon patterns, glacial melt, sea-level rise, and groundwater depletion. • Physico-chemical and biological parameters of water (turbidity, pH, DO, BOD, COD, TDS, heavy metals, microbial load). • Emerging contaminants: Microplastics, pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs), endocrine disruptors, PFAS (forever chemicals) – sources, pathways, and risks. • Water quality indices (WQI) and their applications. 4

units.title: Water Pollution: Contemporary Issues
units.topics: • Point and non-point source pollution – agricultural runoff (fertilisers, pesticides), industrial effluents, urban stormwater. • Eutrophication and harmful algal blooms (HABs): Causes, consequences (dead zones), case studies (Loktak Lake, Vembanad Lake). • Groundwater contamination: Arsenic, Fluoride, Nitrate, and Salinity intrusion – Indian case studies (West Bengal, Assam, Rajasthan, Punjab). • River pollution in India: Status of Ganga, Yamuna, Godavari, Cauvery – pollution hotspots and source apportionment. • Waterborne diseases: Cholera, Typhoid, Hepatitis A, and emerging water-related health risks (antibiotic resistance in water systems). • Water stress, water conflict, and environmental justice.

units.title: Modern Water Pollution Management
units.topics: • Water quality standards: BIS (IS 10500:2012), WHO, CPCB standards for drinking, bathing, and industrial uses. • Advanced water treatment technologies: - Primary, Secondary (activated sludge, biofilm reactors), Tertiary treatment (membrane filtration, reverse osmosis, UV, advanced oxidation processes). - Nature-based solutions: Constructed wetlands, phytoremediation, riverbank filtration. • Decentralised wastewater treatment: STPs, FSTP (faecal sludge treatment plants), and reuse of treated water (circular economy). • Legal framework: Water (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act, 1974; National Water Policy; Central and State Pollution Control Boards. • Flagship programs: Namami Gange Mission, National River Conservation Plan (NRCP), Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT). • Application of GIS, Remote Sensing, and AI/ML for water quality monitoring, pollution source tracking, and flood/drought management.

units.title: Soil Health, Degradation and Emerging Contaminants
units.topics: • Soil: Definition, formation, composition (mineral, organic matter, water, air). • Soil health vs soil fertility: Indicators of soil health (physical, chemical, biological). • Soil reactions: pH, buffering capacity, CEC, salinity, and sodicity. • Macro and micronutrients (NPK, S, Zn, Fe, B) – deficiency symptoms and management. • Emerging soil contaminants: Microplastics, pharmaceutical residues, heavy metals (Cd, Pb, As, Hg), e-waste leachates, and perchlorates. • Soil acidification, salinisation, and alkalization – causes and reclamation methods. • Soil degradation: Soil erosion (water, wind), desertification, loss of organic carbon, and soil biodiversity decline. 5

units.title: Soil Pollution, Remediation and Sustainable Management
units.topics: • Sources of soil pollution: Industrial waste, mining, agricultural chemicals (pesticides, fertilisers), urban solid waste (landfills, leachates), and untreated wastewater irrigation. • Soil toxicology: Impact on soil microbiota, plants, and human health (food chain contamination). • Remediation technologies: - Physical: Soil washing, thermal desorption. - Chemical: Chemical oxidation, stabilisation/solidification. - Biological: Bioremediation (bioaugmentation, biostimulation), phytoremediation (phytoextraction, rhizofiltration), mycoremediation. - Nature-based solutions: Biochar application, green amendments. • Soil conservation techniques: Contour farming, strip cropping, terracing, agroforestry, conservation tillage, cover cropping. • Government initiatives: Soil Health Card Scheme, National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA), Organic farming promotion. • Application of GIS, remote sensing, and AI for soil mapping, erosion risk assessment, and precision agriculture. • Integrated Water-Soil Management (IWSM) for climate resilience, carbon sequestration, and achieving SDG 6 & 15.

units.title: The Atmosphere: Structure and Greenhouse Effect
units.topics: • What is atmosphere? Importance of atmosphere for life on Earth. • Layers of atmosphere: Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, Thermosphere (basic features only). • Composition of air: Nitrogen, Oxygen, Carbon dioxide, water vapour, and other gases. • Solar radiation and heat balance of Earth. • Greenhouse effect: What is it? Natural vs enhanced greenhouse effect. • Greenhouse gases (GHGs): CO₂, Methane (CH₄), Nitrous oxide (N₂O), Water vapour – their sources (natural and artificial). • Simple concept of Global Warming Potential (GWP).

units.title: Atmospheric Circulation and Weather Systems
units.topics: • Wind systems: What causes wind? High and low-pressure areas. • Global wind patterns: Trade winds, Westerlies, Jet streams (basic idea). • Cyclones and Anticyclones: How they form; tropical cyclones (examples: Cyclone Tauktae, Cyclone Amphan). • Ocean effects on climate: El Niño and La Niña – meaning and effects on the Indian climate. • Indian Monsoon: What is monsoon? How does it form? Onset and retreat of monsoon in India. 7 • Effect of monsoon on Indian agriculture and economy. • Urban heat island: Why cities are warmer than villages (simple explanation).

units.title: Basic Meteorology and Air Quality
units.topics: • Weather vs. Climate: Difference between weather and climate. • Important weather terms: Temperature, humidity, wind speed & direction, rainfall, air pressure. • Temperature inversion: What is it? Why does it happen? How does it trap pollutants (e.g., winter smog in Delhi). • Atmospheric stability: Stable vs. unstable air – simple understanding. • Air Quality Index (AQI): What is AQI? Different categories (Good, Moderate, Poor, Very Poor, Severe). • Air pollution episodes in Indian cities (Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata). • Basic idea of how pollutants disperse in air (plume behavior – simple description).

units.title: Global Warming and Climate Change: Causes & Impacts
units.topics: • Global warming: What is it? Rising global temperatures (simple data: Earth has warmed about 1.2°C since pre-industrial times). • Causes of global warming: Burning of fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas), deforestation, agriculture, industrial activities. • Observed changes: Melting of glaciers (Himalayan glaciers), shrinking Arctic sea ice, rising sea levels. • Impacts of climate change in India: - More frequent heatwaves (example: 2022, 2023 heatwaves in North India). - Changes in monsoon pattern (delayed monsoon, heavy rainfall events, floods). - Droughts in some regions (Marathwada, Bundelkhand). - Effect on farming (wheat, rice, sugarcane yields). - Sea level rise threat to coastal cities (Mumbai, Chennai, Sundarbans). - Health effects: Heat strokes, spread of diseases (malaria, dengue). - Glacial lake outburst floods (GLOF) – example: Sikkim 2023 flood.

units.title: Climate Policy and India's Climate Action
units.topics: • International efforts to control climate change: - Montreal Protocol (1987), Kyoto Protocol (1997) Paris Agreement (2015), Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). • Simple concepts: Carbon credit, Carbon trading, Clean Development Mechanism 8 (CDM). • India's climate commitments and• India's major climate programs (simple overview): - National Solar Mission (promoting solar energy). - National Water Mission (water conservation). - National Mission for Green India (increase forest cover). - National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (climate-resilient farming). • Simple case studies: - Solar energy success in India (example: Bhadla Solar Park, Rajasthan). - Climate-resilient farming in rainfed areas (example: Andhra Pradesh). - Mumbai Climate Action Plan (basic idea).

subjects.title: Practicals based on EVS 301 MJ and EVS 302 MJ

units.title: Terrestrial Ecology
units.topics: • Introduction to Terrestrial Environment. • Parameters of terrestrial environment (climatic, edaphic, topographic, biotic). • The terrestrial biota and biogeographic regions of India (Trans-Himalayan, Himalayan, Desert, Semi-arid, Western Ghats, Deccan Peninsula, Gangetic Plain, Coasts, North-East, Islands). • The Soil subsystem – soil formation, profile, types, and soil biota. • Biodiversity hotspots in India: Western Ghats, Eastern Himalayas, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Sundaland (Nicobar component). •IUCN Red List 2024-25 status of Indian terrestrial species.

units.title: Terrestrial Biodiversity
units.topics: • Introduction and concept of biodiversity. • Types of biomes: Tropical rainforest, tropical deciduous forest, temperate forest, taiga, tundra, grassland, savanna, desert, Mediterranean. • Biogeographic regions of the world (Palaearctic, Nearctic, Neotropical, Afrotropical, Indomalayan, Australasian, Oceanian, Antarctic). 12 • General structure of terrestrial communities – stratification, edge effect, ecotone. • Distribution patterns of species (cosmopolitan, endemic, disjunct). • Keystone species – concept and examples (Indian elephant, fig trees, tigers, bees). • Interspecies relationships: Competition, predation, parasitism, mutualism, commensalism, amensalism.

units.title: Terrestrial Ecosystem Services
units.topics: • Definition and classification of ecosystem services (Millennium Ecosystem Assessment – provisioning, regulating, cultural, supporting). • Aesthetic and cultural benefits – sacred groves, cultural landscapes, and traditional knowledge. • Tourism and recreation – eco-tourism, wildlife tourism, carrying capacity. • Industrial products – timber, non-timber forest products (NTFP), resins, gums, medicinal plants. • Drugs and medicines – phytopharmaceuticals, traditional medicine systems (Ayurveda, Siddha, Ethnobotany). • Carbon pool and sequestration potential – forest carbon stocks, blue carbon, REDD+ mechanism. • Case studies: Sacred groves of Western Ghats (Kavus of Kerala, Devrais of Maharashtra).

units.title: Methods of Terrestrial Ecosystem Management
units.topics: • Remote sensing – principles, satellite data sources (Landsat, Sentinel, IRS), applications in forest cover mapping. • Geographical Information System (GIS) – spatial analysis, land use/land cover (LULC) mapping, habitat suitability modelling. • Community-based forest management – Joint Forest Management (JFM), Community Forest Rights (FRA 2006), Van Panchayats. • Traditional methods – sacred groves, traditional water harvesting, shifting cultivation (Jhum) – benefits and challenges. • Forest fire – reasons (natural and anthropogenic), effects (on biodiversity, soil, air quality), control measures (fire lines, controlled burning, early warning systems), and management. •National Action Plan on Forest Fires (NAPFF), Forest Fire Alert System (FAST).

units.title: Exploitation and Sustainable Utilization
units.topics: • Reasons for exploitation: Population growth, poverty, market demand, weak enforcement. • Threats of exploitation: Deforestation, habitat fragmentation, poaching, illegal wildlife trade, overgrazing, invasive species. • Sustainable management methods: Sustainable forest management (SFM), certification (FSC), participatory forest management, landscape approach. • Role of People, NGOs, Community, and Local Government in conservation. • Community Based terrestrial ecosystem management 13 methods – village forest committees, eco-development committees, biodiversity management committees (BMC). • Case studies: - Chipko Movement (Uttarakhand) - Appiko Movement (Karnataka) - Joint Forest Management in West Bengal (Arabari model) - Community conservation of Great Indian Bustard in Maharashtra (Nannaj).

units.title: Introduction to Wildlife Biology
units.topics: • Introduction to Wildlife Biology. • Definition of Wildlife Biology. • Study of characteristics of wildlife habitats: - Aquatic Habitat: Marine, Freshwater, Estuaries. - Terrestrial Habitat: Forest, Grassland, Desert, Landscape.

units.title: Groups of Wildlife Species
units.topics: • Plant Classification: Algae, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms, Angiosperms (Monocot and Dicot). • Animal Classification: - Arthropods (Insects, Arachnids, Crustaceans, Millipedes, Centipedes). - Vertebrates (Mammals, Birds, Fish, Reptiles, Amphibians).

units.title: Threats to Wildlife
units.topics: • Habitat Destruction. • Developmental Projects and Urbanization. • Agriculture expansion. • Poaching and Deforestation. • Human-Wildlife Conflict. • Exploitation of animals and plants.

units.title: Habitat Analysis and Population Assessment Techniques
units.topics: • Standard Evaluation processes for habitat: HEP & HIS. • Population Assessment techniques (Wildlife Census): - Direct count: Block count, Transect methods, Point count, Visual encounter survey, Waterhole survey. - Indirect count: Pugmark, Camera trap, DNA fingerprinting, Call count, Track and sign, Pellet 15 count. - Marking wildlife: Ringing, Tagging, Clipping, Colouring.

units.title: Modern and Sustainable Wildlife Management
units.topics: • Modern Wildlife management techniques: Bio- telemetry. • Management practices: Monitoring Wildlife Populations, Habitat Improvement, Hunting Regulations, Artificial Stocking, Disease Control, Management Funds, Captive breeding and propagation. • Sustainable Wildlife management: Eco-tourism / Wildlife tourism in forests. • Reasons for biodiversity formation, contribution to adaptive evolution. • Landraces of crop plants, conservation of genetic resources.

units.title: Introduction to Law and Policy
units.topics: • Concept of law and policy. • Environmental governance – importance and elements. • Environmental ethics – introduction, concept, development.

units.title: Constitutional Provisions
units.topics: • Article 48A: Protection and improvement of environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife. • Fundamental Rights and Duties as per the Constitution of India. • Legal definitions: Environmental pollution, natural resource, biodiversity, forest, sustainable development.

units.title: Government Institutions
units.topics: • Role of Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change (MoEFCC). • Role of Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). • Role of State Pollution Control Boards (SPCB). • Role of National Green Tribunal (NGT).

units.title: Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs)
units.topics: • Introduction to GMOs. • Principles and advantages. • Biosafety measures. • Examples of GMOs (Bt cotton, Golden Rice, etc.). • Risks to environment and human health. • Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety.

units.title: Agricultural Biotechnology and Biofertilizers
units.topics: • Introduction to agricultural biotechnology. • Detection and diagnosis of plant diseases. • Micropropagation – principles and applications. • Biofertilizers – types (Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospirillum, Blue Green Algae, Mycorrhiza). • Role of biofertilizers in sustainable agriculture. • Waste utilization in agriculture.

units.title: Microbes in Environmental Biotechnology
units.topics: • Collection and enumeration of microbes from environmental samples. • Ecological relationships of microbes in nature. 25 • Nutritional requirements of microbes. • Nutrient media – types, preparation, and uses. • Isolation and culturing techniques.

units.title: Atmosphere and its Nature
units.topics: • Composition of Atmosphere – permanent and variable gases. • Chemical and photochemical reactions in the atmosphere. • Human activities and meteorology. • Factors influencing the pollutant mix in the atmosphere. • Transport of Pollution in Atmosphere. • Global Warming, Ozone Hole, El Niño, La Niña Phenomenon.

units.title: Air Pollution
units.topics: • Air pollution – meaning and definition. • Sources and types of air pollutants (primary and secondary). • Major air pollutants – SO₂, NOx, CO, O₃, PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, Pb, VOCs. • Types of air pollution – indoor air pollution, vehicular pollution, industrial pollution. • Status of Air pollution in India. • Effects of air pollution on plants, animals, humans, and materials. 27 • Smog (photochemical and classical) and Acid rain. • Control of air pollution – preventive and control measures. • Emission Standards (Bharat Stage VI). • Air Quality Index (AQI) and Air Pollution Tolerance Index (APTI).

units.title: Analytical Methods for Monitoring Air Pollutants
units.topics: • Sampling methods for air pollutants – grab sampling, continuous sampling. • Stack sampling – principles and equipment. • Instrumentation and methods of analysis: - SO₂ – Modified West & Gaeke method. - CO – Non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) method. - NOx – Jacob & Hochheiser method. - Hydrogen Sulphide (H₂S) – Methylene blue method. - Hydrocarbons – Flame ionization detector (FID). - Methane – Gas chromatography. - Particulate Matter – Gravimetric method (High Volume Sampler, Fine Particulate Sampler).

units.title: Air Pollution Control
units.topics: • Air pollution control – at source. • Equipment for control of air pollution – For Particulate Matter: - Settling chambers. - Fabric filters (Baghouses). - Scrubbers (Venturi, Spray tower). - Cyclones. - Electrostatic Precipitators (ESP). • Equipment for control of Gaseous pollutants: - Absorption. - Adsorption. - Scrubbers (chemical scrubbing).

units.title: Noise Pollution – Basics and Acoustics
units.topics: • Basics of acoustics and specification of sound. • Sound power, sound intensity, and sound pressure levels. • Plane, point, and line sources; multiple sources. • Causes of noise – industrial, vehicular, construction, domestic, aviation. • Outdoor and indoor noise propagation. • Psycho-acoustics and noise criteria. • Noise instrumentation – Sound Level Meter (SLM) – components and working. • Noise monitoring procedure – sampling techniques, duration, frequency.

units.title: Noise Pollution – Effects, Indices and Control
units.topics: • Effects of noise on health – hearing loss (temporary and permanent), cardiovascular effects, sleep disturbance, annoyance, stress, communication interference. • Annoyance rating schemes. • Special noise environments – Infra-sound, ultrasound, impulsive sound, sonic boom. • Noise indices – L₁₀, L₅₀, L₉₀, Leq (Equivalent Continuous Noise Level), Ldn (Day-Night Level), LNP (Noise Pollution Level). • Noise standards and limit values (CPCB, WHO, IS 9876). • Noise control techniques – source control, path control, 28 receiver control. • Acoustic zoning and noise barriers. • Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 (India).

units.title: Limnology

units.title: Distribution of Major Aquatic Ecosystems
units.topics: • Classification of aquatic ecosystems – freshwater, marine, estuarine. • Structure and patterns of aquatic ecosystems. • Types of interactions in aquatic communities. • Stratification and Zonation in lakes and oceans. • Impact of Climate change on aquatic ecosystems.

units.title: Freshwater Ecology
units.topics: • The freshwater environment – types (lentic and lotic). • Limiting factors in freshwater ecosystems. • Ecological classification of freshwater organisms. • Freshwater biota (flora and fauna). • Lentic communities – lakes and ponds (littoral, limnetic, profundal zones). • Lotic communities – rivers, streams, springs. • Planktons – phytoplankton and zooplankton. • Biodiversity, negative and positive feedbacks, and resilience.

units.title: Marine and Estuarine Ecology
units.topics: • The marine environment – characteristics and zones. • Marine biota (flora and fauna). • Zonation in the sea – intertidal, neritic, oceanic, benthic zones. 34 • Study of planktons in marine ecosystems. • Communities in the marine environment. • Food production potential of marine ecosystems. • Mangrove Vegetation – types, distribution, ecological significance. • Coral reefs – types, formation, threats, and conservation. • Ecological significance of mangroves and coral reefs.

units.title: Aquatic Ecosystem Management
units.topics: • Methods of aquatic ecosystem management: - Remote sensing and GIS applications. - Eco-development programs. - Traditional methods of water conservation (e.g., stepwells, tanks, kunds). • Methods of aquatic sampling and data analysis – sampling approaches, species association. • Exploitation and consequences of wetlands. • Sustainable management of aquatic resources. • Role of Local Government and people in conservation. • Impact of Tourism and Eco-tourism on aquatic ecosystems. • Conservation and Sustainable use of India's aquatic resources. • Case studies (e.g., Loktak Lake, Chilika Lake, Vembanad Lake, Sundarbans).

units.title: Introduction to Nature Conservation
units.topics: • Introduction to Nature Conservation. • Concept of nature conservation. • Objectives of nature conservation – preservation, restoration, sustainable use. • Challenges in nature conservation – habitat loss, climate change, poaching, human-wildlife conflict.

units.title: In-situ Conservation
units.topics: • Concept and principles of In-situ Conservation. • Types of in-situ conservation: - Biosphere reserves (structure – core, buffer, transition zones). - National Parks. - Wildlife Sanctuaries. - Biodiversity Hotspots. - Gene Sanctuaries. - Community Reserves. - Conservation Reserves. - Sacred Groves. • Challenges, merits, and demerits of in-situ conservation.

units.title: Ex-situ Conservation
units.topics: • Concept and principles of Ex-situ Conservation. • Types of ex-situ conservation: - Cryopreservation (preservation at very low temperatures). - Seed banks (storage of seeds). - Field gene banks (living collections). - Cultivation collections (botanical gardens, zoos, aquariums). - Tissue culture and micropropagation. • Challenges, merits, and demerits of ex-situ conservation.

units.title: International and National Efforts for Conservation
units.topics: • International efforts: - Role of IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature) – Red List, protected area categories. - Role of WWF (World Wide Fund for Nature). - Introduction to Protocols and Conventions – CITES, Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), Ramsar Convention, Bonn Convention. • National efforts: - BNHS (Bombay Natural History Society). - Conservation missions – Project Tiger, Project Elephant, Crocodile Conservation, Rhino Conservation, Reindeer Conservation, Whaling mission. - Administrative setup – MoEFCC, CPCB, SPCB, National Board for Wildlife (NBWL). - Role of NGOs in nature conservation.

units.title: Introduction to Remote Sensing
units.topics: • Definition and principles of Remote Sensing. • Components of Remote Sensing – Energy source, target, sensor, processing, application. • Types of Remote Sensing – Active and Passive Remote Sensing. • Electromagnetic spectrum (Gamma rays to Radio waves). • Refraction, Reflectance, Emission, and Scattering. • Atmospheric windows.

units.title: Satellites and Sensors

units.title: Introduction to GIS

units.title: Applications of Remote Sensing and GIS
